definition: A prostitute or sex worker; an archaic literary term in classical and formal Modern Standard Arabic for a woman who sells sexual services.
notes: More literary and dated than colloquial equivalents; appears in formal texts, journalism, and classical literature rather than street speech; less loaded than قحبة or شرموطة.

definition: A prostitute or harlot; a Quranic and classical Arabic term for a woman who engages in unlawful sexual relations for pay, carrying strong religious and moral condemnation.
notes: Quranic term (24:33) used for a woman forced into or practicing prostitution; retains heavy religious framing in modern MSA usage; moralistic charge absent from clinical equivalents; root بغي connotes transgression and injustice.

definition: The most common crude vulgar term for a prostitute or whore across Arabic dialects; used both as a literal designation for sex workers and as a general misogynistic insult targeting any woman.
notes: One of the most offensive Arabic words for a woman; crosses freely from literal sex-work reference into general slut-shaming; widely understood across all Arabic-speaking regions regardless of dialect.

definition: An extremely crude slur for a promiscuous woman, slut, or whore; among the most intensely offensive Arabic terms for female sexual immorality, deployed both literally and as a maximally derogatory all-purpose insult.
notes: Rivals قحبة in vulgarity; somewhat more common in Levantine and Egyptian dialects as a slut-shaming term than a strict sex-work designation; among the harshest things one can call an Arabic-speaking woman; etymology uncertain, possibly Aramaic or Turkish.

definition: Prostitution or sex work as a social and legal phenomenon; the standard Modern Standard Arabic clinical and journalistic term for the practice of exchanging sex for money.
notes: Default MSA term in law, journalism, and public health; not particularly crude due to formal register, though the subject carries cultural stigma; appears in compounds such as بيت الدعارة (brothel) and شبكة دعارة (prostitution ring).

definition: A brothel or house of prostitution; the standard compound noun in Modern Standard Arabic legal, journalistic, and formal contexts for a premises where commercial sex is conducted.
notes: Literal translation: 'house of prostitution.' Standard MSA phrase used in legislation, law-enforcement reporting, and journalism throughout the Arab world; clinical register despite referring to an illicit institution.

definition: A brothel or house of ill repute; a more literary and classical Arabic compound for a brothel, drawing on the Quranic term بغيّ (harlot) rather than the modern clinical دعارة.
notes: More archaic and literary than بيت الدعارة; appears in classical texts and older journalism; carries stronger religious and moral overtones due to the Quranic root بغي; less common in contemporary MSA usage.

definition: A pimp or procurer who manages sex workers and profits from their earnings; also used as a general insult for a contemptible, dishonorable, or opportunistic man.
notes: Root قاد (to lead) frames this as 'leader of prostitutes'; doubles as a common insult meaning roughly 'dishonorable opportunist' with no strict sex-work implication; widely understood across Arabic dialects.

definition: A pimp, procurer, or man who profits from or facilitates prostitution; also a crude insult for an effeminate, passive, or morally debased man, especially one perceived as homosexual.
notes: Predominantly Egyptian and Levantine colloquial; carries heavy honor-shame connotations beyond the sex-work meaning; also deployed as a homophobic insult for a passive gay man; extremely offensive on multiple cultural axes simultaneously.

definition: A streetwalker or sex worker who solicits clients in public; literally 'snatcher,' evoking the image of a woman who seizes passersby for sexual business.
notes: Primarily Egyptian colloquial; the literal meaning 'snatcher/kidnapper' is repurposed as a vivid metaphor for street solicitation; not widely used in formal MSA contexts or outside Egypt and the Levant.

definition: A colloquial and derogatory Egyptian Arabic term for a red-light district or neighborhood known for prostitution; literally 'donkey alley,' evoking baseness and animalistic degradation.
notes: Highly colloquial Egyptian slang; the donkey (ḥimār) metaphor implies brutishness and sexual availability as degradation; not used in formal or pan-Arabic contexts; name may also reference specific historical Cairo neighborhoods.

definition: Pornography or pornographic material; the standard Modern Standard Arabic term for explicit sexual content, derived from the root أباح (to permit), ironically invoking permissibility for content widely considered forbidden.
notes: Used in law, journalism, and content regulation; relatively clinical despite its subject matter; the root أباح (to permit/make lawful) creates an interesting semantic tension given that such content is legally and religiously prohibited across most Arab states.

definition: Pornographic films; the standard MSA compound noun for filmed sexually explicit content, used in legal, journalistic, and regulatory contexts throughout the Arab world.
notes: Literal translation: 'permissive/pornographic films'; standard in legislation and media reporting; less loaded than colloquial alternatives; widely understood across all Arabic-speaking regions; frequently appears in criminal statutes and content-moderation policy.

definition: Pornographic material or explicit sexual content in any medium; a broad compound noun used in legal and journalistic contexts to cover films, images, and digital content collectively.
notes: The prompt romanizes this as 'mādd' (singular) but the Arabic مواد is plural (mawādd, 'materials/substances'); the plural broadens the term to encompass any medium; standard in Arab-state legislation banning explicit content and in platform content-moderation policy.

definition: Commercial sex or the transactional exchange of sexual services for money; a clinical MSA phrase used in public health, human rights, and social-science discourse on sex work.
notes: Formal clinical compound that deliberately avoids moral framing; common in UN and NGO reports written in or translated into Arabic; less common in street-level discourse than دعارة; carries a neutral bureaucratic register.

definition: Body rental; a euphemistic or polemical phrase describing the purchase of sexual services, framing sex work as the temporary hire of a human body rather than naming the sexual act directly.
notes: Not standard terminology; appears in polemical, religious, and feminist Arabic discourse to describe or critique sex work; the commodification framing (rental rather than sale) is rhetorically charged and appears more in opinion writing than in legislation or everyday speech.

definition: A sexual broker, procurer, or intermediary who arranges sex work transactions, functioning as a pimp, trafficker, or agent connecting clients with sex workers.
notes: سمسار is the standard Arabic word for broker or middleman (real estate, stock market); combining it with جنسي (sexual) creates a formal, somewhat euphemistic compound that appears in legal and journalistic contexts rather than colloquial speech.

definition: The sex trade or sex industry as a commercial and social institution; a formal MSA compound for the organized commercial exchange of sexual services.
notes: Literal translation: 'commerce of sex'; used in human rights reporting, anti-trafficking legislation, and academic Arabic texts; more neutral in framing than moralistic alternatives like دعارة; common in pan-Arab media coverage of trafficking.

definition: Sexual exploitation; a formal legal and human rights term for the coercive use of persons for sexual purposes, encompassing trafficking, forced prostitution, and abuse of power differentials.
notes: Standard MSA legal and NGO terminology; broader than sex trafficking alone (which implies transport and recruitment) but mapped there as closest registry concept; appears in UN conventions in Arabic translation, domestic legislation, and regional media covering trafficking and abuse.

definition: A male condom; the formal Modern Standard Arabic clinical term for a penile sheath contraceptive, literally meaning 'male protector' or 'male shield.'
notes: Preferred in public health communications and medical contexts; واقٍ means 'protector/shield' (active participle of وقى, to protect) and ذكري means 'male'; less common in colloquial speech where loanwords or عازل dominate depending on region.

definition: A colloquial loanword for condom, borrowed from French 'capote'; used primarily in North African and Levantine colloquial Arabic among French-influenced Maghrebi speakers.
notes: From French 'capote' (literally 'hood'); strongest in Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, and Lebanon due to French colonial linguistic legacy; less familiar in Gulf or Egyptian Arabic where عازل or واقٍ ذكري are preferred; carries a slightly casual or street-level register relative to clinical MSA alternatives.

definition: A condom or barrier contraceptive; derived from the Arabic root عزل (to isolate or insulate), used in both clinical and everyday speech as a relatively neutral term for a condom.
notes: The root عزل (isolation/insulation) gives this a physical-barrier framing analogous to an electrical insulator; used in health campaigns and colloquial speech; more widely understood across dialects than واقٍ ذكري but less colloquially embedded than كابوت in the Maghreb.

definition: Pregnancy; the condition of carrying a developing fetus in the uterus; the standard Modern Standard Arabic term for pregnancy across all registers from clinical to everyday speech.
notes: حمل also means 'carrying/bearing' in non-reproductive senses (e.g., carrying a load), giving it a mild euphemistic quality in reproductive contexts; universally understood; no registry equivalent exists, hence novel concept flag despite a direct English translation.

definition: Abortion or miscarriage; the termination of a pregnancy whether spontaneous or induced; the standard Modern Standard Arabic clinical and legal term used in medical, religious, and legislative discourse.
notes: Arabic إجهاض covers both spontaneous miscarriage and induced abortion without distinguishing them lexically, unlike English; context determines meaning; heavily charged in Islamic jurisprudence and subject to legal restriction across most Arab states; marked novel because no registry entry covers this concept.

definition: Contraception or birth control; the standard Modern Standard Arabic compound for methods used to prevent pregnancy, literally 'prevention of pregnancy.'
notes: Literal translation: 'prevention of pregnancy'; used in public health, medical, and NGO family-planning contexts; neutral clinical register; widely used across the Arab world in family planning campaigns and reproductive health discourse.
